title: What Battle Cards is now
subtitle: Notes from building an AI lab that rolls up creative studios, so the internet isn't full of slop. Read this first.

content.text: Battle Cards started in 2020 as a newsletter about building deep-tech products, mostly augmented reality, written in the gap after Scapic was acquired by Flipkart. The idea was to write down the tactical, unglamorous lessons I wished someone had handed me when I started: screenshot-sized, built to be used rather than admired.
A lot has changed since then, both in my work and in the world. So it seems worth explaining what Battle Cards is now, and why you might want to read it.
What I'm building
I'm building ShopOS: an AI lab that rolls up creative studios, so that the internet isn't full of slop.

That sentence has two halves, and both matter. The first is that creative work still needs people. The best studios, the ones that shoot the catalogue, make the ads and build the brand, have something that is very hard to copy: taste, judgement and years of knowing what actually sells. The second is that AI is about to flood every channel with content that has none of that. Generation is now nearly free. Judgement isn't.

Our bet is that the winners will be studios whose taste runs at the speed of software. That means writing down what a great studio knows, as skill files, guides, critics and rules, putting models inside that environment, and letting the humans spend their time on the hard calls. We buy and build alongside the studios that are already great, and give them one shared memory and one media engine underneath.
What you'll get
There are three kinds of posts on Battle Cards now.
Battle cards.
The original format, back again: one idea, two reasons, three things to do, sized to fit on a phone. The first set is twelve lessons from twelve years and four exits.
Long essays.

Slower, deeper pieces about how AI is changing creative work, brands and commerce. The current series is Brands Are RL Environments, which argues that slop is what happens when nobody designs the world a model works inside, and walks through two experiments step by step.
Experiments.

We regularly test what new models can do when they are given a real job and a well-designed environment: start a cloud kitchen, launch a car perfume, study a new browser. I'll share what came back, what worked, what broke, and the files behind it. Most of them also live on GitHub.

A bit about me

I've been building startups for twelve years. Four of them have been acquired: Scapic by Flipkart, Cope.Studio by Polygon, Reality Tools by MotionPage, and Dehidden by Layer-E. I hold more than fifteen patents in deep tech, co-founded SeeIt, an open-source AI smart glasses lab, and am a double graduate of Stanford GSB. These days my title on ShopOS writing is Chief Janitor, which is more accurate than it sounds.

If something on Battle Cards is useful, the best thing you can do is forward it to one person who is building something. And if you are running a studio or a brand and want to try any of this on your own work, reply. I read everything.
